text: Yes, our city should adopt a carbon price, and I think the local bus depot and the gas plant on the east side are the clearest reasons why. Right now those operators pay nothing for the smoke they put over my neighborhood, so cleaning up is always the option that costs them more. A modest fee on each ton of carbon flips that math, because suddenly the cheaper choice is the cleaner one. The objection I hear most is that the fee just lands on regular families through higher heating and gas bills, and honestly that worry is fair. My answer is that the city should hand the money straight back as a quarterly rebate split evenly per resident. Households that already drive less or live in smaller places would actually come out ahead, while the heaviest polluters carry the real weight. I will admit a carbon price alone will not fix everything, since we still need better bus routes and cleaner buildings. But it is a fair, simple lever the council can pull this year, and waiting for a perfect plan usually means doing nothing. We should start the fee small, publish the results, and raise it only if the air does not improve.
